Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. As Fintrax starts mapping Redwood into our incident response, Legal asked me to capture a couple of clarifying asks related to the DPA and how you coordinate with subprocessors in the event of a privacy/security incident. High level: timelines, evidence scope, and whether transfers to subprocessor-controlled environments (including cross-border transfers) are supported.

Specifics we need for procurement & Security:
- Confirmation of your"notification window" for confirmed incidents vs preliminary alerts (we typically contract 24-72 hours depending on severity).
- What evidence you can provide (e.g., hashes, logs, forensic images) and what redaction/PII masking you apply prior to transfer.
- Your process for handing evidence when the impacted data is stored or processed by a subprocessor (do you coordinate, take responsibility, or facilitate direct handoff?).
- Whether you can host evidence in an EU data escrow or provide a secure transfer mechanism compatible with our legal hold.

I've attached a short doc with our regulatory constraints and the DPA excerpts we reference. Please respond with what you can commit to contractually vs operationally. We need a short note for our GC by EOW.

Hi Maria — thanks for the note and the doc. Looping in Lauren (Head of Privacy) and Ben (Subprocessor Ops) so they see the ask. Below are the operational commitments we can make today and language we typically accept in the DPA; we'll flag anything that requires Legal review.

1) Notification windows
- Preliminary alert: we commit to an initial operational alert within 24 hours of first identifying an event that plausibly impacts customer data (this will include high-level scope and whether the event meets our incident criteria).
- Confirmed incident notification: for incidents we confirm as meeting the DPA "security incident" definition, we commit to notifying customers within 72 hours of confirmation.
- Escalations: if regulators or law enforcement request accelerated notice, we will notify customers within 24 hours of becoming aware of the request and will cooperate on messaging.

2) Evidence & scope
- We can provide structured logs, redacted exports, and cryptographic hashes of forensic images. Full disk images or raw memory dumps are treated as high-sensitivity and will require an explicit forensic request and an agreed AkA chain-of-custody.
- PII redaction: we can provide redacted artifacts by default and will work with Fintrax to produce tokenized or hashed samples where feasible to preserve investigatory value while minimizing shared PII.

3) Subprocessor coordination & handoff
- If the impacted processing was performed by a subprocessor, Redwood will: (a) coordinate the collection of artifacts from that subprocessor; (b) facilitate transfer to an agreed secure endpoint (S3 presigned, encrypted SFTP, or mutually agreed escrow); and (c) where contractually required, use reasonable commercial efforts to obtain artifacts directly from the subprocessor.
- We cannot unilaterally force a subprocessor to release materials beyond what is allowed by their agreements, but we will escalate contractually and operationally to get timely access. Where access is delayed, we commit to providing Fintrax with interim artifacts (summaries, hashes, timeline of events).

4) Cross-border / escrow options
- We can stage evidence in an EU-located escrow (customer-provided account) or provide encrypted exports delivered via an EU-hosted transfer when EU residency is required.

We've attached a short Incident Response SLA describing timelines and standard handoff methods. If this matches Fintrax needs, we can convert the key bullets into proposed DPA language for your GC.

Next steps: Lauren, Ben — can you confirm there are no blockers to the above, and Ben, can you validate the escrow/transfer options operationally? Maria — if you can confirm which EU jurisdiction and the preferred evidence hosting approach, we'll draft language for review.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Marcus — thank you, this is helpful. A few follow-ups based on our internal regulators: 

- For EU-resident customers (GDPR focus) we need: preliminary alert within 12 hours for incidents likely affecting EU personal data, and confirmed notification within 48 hours where feasible. Is Redwood able to commit to accelerated timing for EU-scoped events?

- On evidence: we prefer receiving hashed samples + redacted logs initially. In cases where that is insufficient, we will request limited, scoped forensic artifacts under an agreed chain-of-custody. Can you confirm Redwood will accept a mutually signed COC and transfer artifacts to an EU-hosted escrow?

- Subprocessor accountability: our standard DPA includes a clause requiring the vendor to secure equivalent obligations from subprocessors and to "use commercially reasonable efforts" to obtain artifacts. We need clarity on whether Redwood will accept contractual language that requires remedial steps if a subprocessor delays or refuses cooperation.

Attached is a short summary of the regulatory asks for Fintrax. We need a one-page summary for procurement by Friday COB so please advise on any redlines.

Best,
Maria

Maria — appreciate the specificity. Below is a concise summary we can pass to GC and Procurement; I've also sketched proposed contract language (attached) for your legal team to review. Lauren and Ben, please confirm and flag anything operationally impossible.

Summary (for Fintrax procurement):
- Preliminary alert: Redwood will provide an initial incident alert within 24 hours for global incidents; for incidents that are confirmed to impact EU personal data, Redwood will accelerate the preliminary alert to 12 hours where practicable and include an initial scope estimate.
- Confirmed notice: Redwood commits to providing confirmed incident notification within 72 hours globally; for EU-scoped incidents Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify within 48 hours.
- Evidence: Redwood will deliver redacted logs and cryptographic hashes as the default. If additional forensic artifacts are necessary, Redwood will accept a mutually executed chain-of-custody and transfer artifacts to an EU-hosted escrow or customer-provided secure account.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will require subprocessors to agree to equivalent contractual obligations where possible and will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain evidence from subprocessors. If a subprocessor refuses or delays, Redwood will (a) escalate contractually; (b) provide interim summaries and hashes; and (c) work with Fintrax on remediation steps.

Proposed clause (high level):
"In the event of a Security Incident affecting Customer Personal Data, Vendor shall: (i) provide initial notification within twelve (12) hours for incidents materially affecting EU personal data and within twenty-four (24) hours for other incidents; (ii) provide confirmed notice within forty-eight (48) hours for EU incidents and within seventy-two (72) hours for other incidents; (iii) deliver redacted artifacts and cryptographic hashes by default and, where necessary, deliver additional forensic artifacts pursuant to a mutually executed chain-of-custody and an EU-hosted encrypted transfer; and (iv) require subprocessors to adhere to equivalent obligations and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain evidence from such subprocessors."

We can accept that language subject to Legal review and a short appendix describing acceptable artifact types and transfer mechanisms.

Next step — Lauren / Ben: can we confirm operational feasibility and sign-off so we can send a one-page procurement summary + proposed clause to Fintrax GC by Friday?

Thanks,
Marcus
